title: Interlanguage and Mathematical Translation Methodology Sidecar
description:
This release maintains the interlanguage and mathematical-translation methodology sidecar as a human-readable and reproducible record of the programme's language evidence, source-body baselines, manager handoffs, and normalization workflow.

Read first: 00_Interlanguage_Research_Method_Current_v06_20260718.pdf. It explains the governing evidence distinctions and the controlled Noether Interslavic normalization completed in tranches 002A and 002B.

Current result: the complete extant Noether Interslavic production corpus contains 221 Latin-script and 221 Cyrillic-script canonical TeX units. Tranche 002A changed 146 files under reviewed paired-script orthographic rules. Tranche 002B changed 92 files under exact accepted lexical rules. Both passes were idempotent. Every changed unit compiled, all resulting pages were rendered, and no machine page-quality flag was raised. The evidence package retains exact ledgers, diffs, build and render reports, visual-QA sheets, continuation state, and reusable scripts.

Translation bodies: the complete editable bodies and cumulative readers are published on the Noether record 10.5281/zenodo.21421049 under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20412587. This sidecar publishes method and evidence without duplicating the full corpus.

Status: this is reproducible internal normalization and artifact-quality evidence. It is not native-speaker or community certification, peer review, a critical edition, or mathematical source-fidelity certification. Held and context-sensitive terminology remains open and is documented explicitly.

GitHub: corrections and improved evidence can be suggested through issues or pull requests at https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts.
notes: v0.6 adds the controlled Interslavic normalization method and complete evidence for Noether tranches 002A and 002B. It does not certify language completion, terminology acceptance, native-speaker approval, translation fidelity, mathematical source fidelity, or critical-edition status.
